purpose: Add an explicit opt-in V4 insert-only per-grant custody quarantine, so a recorded uncertainty fence survives normal native SQLite reopen without altering original funding/request/intent bytes.

implementation.exactInput: One own-data grantId field; existing custody-key grammar validates its immutable scope.
implementation.insertOnly: One canonical checksum-bound record per grant. Repeated latches return that same record; no clear, delete, overwrite, reset or migration API is introduced.
binding: Exact stored funding resource URL, payment hash and network
implementation.bound: The number of quarantine rows cannot exceed custodyPolicy.maxRequests; all rows validate before selected reads or writes.
implementation.writeFence: V4 retainOriginalRequest and fenceOriginalDispatchIntent refuse a quarantined grant before inserting or replacing custody/intent rows.
implementation.granularity: Another grant is neither implicitly quarantined nor authorized.
implementation.readBoundary: Existing originals/intents remain readable while the native record is valid. Corrupt quarantine data refuses the whole V4 profile.
implementation.oldProfiles: Existing V1/V2/V3 factories leave the new flag off. V3 and V4 wrong-version files are refused through the fixed read-only SQLite header preflight; no adoption or migration.
implementation.explicitCallerAction: The caller must explicitly latch detected local uncertainty. Existing owners do not automatically write this new record or restore it into their volatile uncertainty flags.
implementation.unchangedDefaults: No buyer, SDK, HTTP client factory, signing path or default activation is switched to V4.
implementation.recordAuthority: NONE; null means no local record, never permission to send or proof of safe recovery.
implementation.notAuthenticated: Checksums and source pins are not authentication against same-UID database mutation.

selection.finiteScope: Four selected tests, one foreground Node command, two new private synthetic SQLite files.
selection.reason: The retained actual-store outcome pins a prior source and demonstrates that a fresh owner starts with false volatile flags after normal reopen. This packet adds a new persistent, grant-scoped write refusal rather than relabeling those old flags or relying on missing coverage as novelty.

sourceBinding.dependencies: Existing request owner, original-request custody contract, x402-wire, pinned package scope and reviewed Node builtins only.

passNames: V4 grant quarantine binds exact funding and idempotent insert-only metadata
normal V4 reopen blocks quarantined grant writes with a fresh existing owner
V4 quarantine capacity and V3 profile refusal preserve closed file bytes
corrupt V4 quarantine metadata is refused before reopen epoch advancement

scenarios.name: V4 grant quarantine binds exact funding and idempotent insert-only metadata
asserts: V4 creation has no quarantine record and cannot latch before any funding pair exists.
A fixed synthetic funding pair reaches BOUND revision 3; an existing V3 owner retains and fences one original.
Explicit quarantine latching is idempotent and independently matches the exact original challenge/payment header digests, policy and checksum.
Original, intent and funding bytes remain unchanged; a quarantined intent write refuses.
Only after closing all production owners does an independent read-only SQL connection inspect the committed row and epoch 1.

scenarios.name: normal V4 reopen blocks quarantined grant writes with a fresh existing owner
asserts: Normal V4 reopen preserves the same quarantine row at epoch 2.
A fresh existing V3 owner still has false volatile flags; those observations are not rewritten.
A new submission for that grant reaches the native quarantine fence, produces no callback/original/intent and latches local UNKNOWN.
A distinct grant with no quarantine uses the existing declared callback path; it is not evidence of real grant or provider authority.
Closing production owners precedes SQL inspection; original grant-A bytes and its quarantine remain exact, funding/schema are unchanged.

scenarios.name: V4 quarantine capacity and V3 profile refusal preserve closed file bytes
asserts: Descriptor-accessor and extra-field inputs reject without invoking the getter.
The four-row configured quarantine capacity is enforced; an existing latch remains idempotent at capacity.
Capacity refusal preserves the existing rows; the absent fifth record grants no authority.
One second new private file is created with the existing V3 factory.
V4-on-V3 and V3-on-V4 opening refuse; complete closed-file bytes and file identities are unchanged.

scenarios.name: corrupt V4 quarantine metadata is refused before reopen epoch advancement
asserts: Only one quarantine envelope in the newly created V4 synthetic file is deliberately corrupted after all production handles are closed.
V4 reopening rejects CORRUPT before owner_epoch advancement.
No corruption repair, replacement, fixture restoration or retry occurs; the intentionally corrupt file remains retained as failure-path evidence.
Original, intent, funding, policy and schema rows remain unchanged.

nativeFiles.corruptionScope: Exactly one new synthetic quarantine envelope; no historical or user database is opened or modified.

callsite.timeoutBoundary: Not a hard native lifetime, cancellation, cleanup, OS or network sandbox guarantee.
callsite.nativeLoaderRunnerStreamOsSqliteAndFiles: Retained premises, not newly qualified global guarantees.

preservation.rawFixtureCleanup: HOLD, not CLEANED. No protected evidence or raw database deleted.
preservation.quotaBoundary: Cooperative sampled accounting, not an OS-enforced aggregate quota.
preservation.runtimeDigests: Reused only after exact unchanged retained runtime identity tuples; no redundant large-binary rehash.

authority.pr193: VALIDATED exact-same-signed-block resend remains distinct from UNKNOWN and ACKNOWLEDGED.

limits: This establishes these four local native SQLite component outcomes only, not complete store, application, SDK or controller qualification.
The explicit caller-recorded grant quarantine survives a normal same-process reopen; automatic detection/latching and client-factory adoption remain unimplemented.
Fresh owner volatile flags are not restored or falsified. Persisted quarantine and owner-local uncertainty remain separate facts.
The V1/V2/V3 unchanged branches are source-reviewed; the selected V3 file/profile checks are not a full legacy regression suite.
No actual process restart, crash, power loss, service delivery, authenticated funding, real provider READY or live pilot was exercised.
The retained V4 fixture intentionally ends with corrupt quarantine metadata; passing the refusal assertion does not make that file a valid recovery store.
Quarantine-row absence and another grant's successful declared callback provide no independent payer/provider/policy authority.
Independent current context, funding, authority, READY, durability, commit/uncertainty and restart/recovery remain separate acceptance gates.
next: Connect explicit uncertainty detection to this opt-in record with source-bound lifecycle tests; keep real process restart and live acceptance separately gated.

publication.packet: One existing opt-in library source plus two new qualification files.
